label: r3c2
name: flip after stem, 64 minibatches
hypothesis: Same network as the flip-after-stem candidate, but with n_minibatches 64 instead of 32. With one epoch, this doubles the gradient steps per sample (64-sample minibatches). Training success levelled off at about 0.85 while the learning rate decayed, so more optimiser steps on the same fresh data should extract more from each sample. Refuted if this is not clearly above the plain flip-after-stem candidate, or if one seed becomes unstable.
last_analysis: The left-right mirror rule is the main obstacle. A fixed flip (in the head, or right after the stem) unlocks learning. A learned column mixer collapsed to DONE. After that, the recipe matters most: going from 2 PPO epochs to 1 means more fresh samples (0.84 to 0.92), and 64 minibatches give more gradient steps per sample (0.897 to 0.949 for the flip-after-stem net). Extra depth hurts: it costs samples, and one deeper seed collapsed to 0.08. gamma 0.99 was unstable. At the best trial's end, training success was still rising (0.91), so the remaining gains probably come from better use of samples or cheap context, not bigger trunks. Seed spread at the top is about ±0.01–0.02, so gains under about 0.02 are not reliable. For this final round I make one change each to the best trial r3c2: a higher learning rate, broadcast global context into the placement head, and a dilated second convolution for a wider view at the same compute.
